evaluatedModels.modelName: Model A: Atomic Exchange Unit (1 User Prompt + 1 Assistant Response)
evaluatedModels.turnWindow: 2 turns (User -> Assistant, including intermediate tool invocations)
strengths: Zero intra-passage topic mixing; pristine topic boundary isolation.
Unambiguous 1:1 attribution to exact message and mapping node IDs.
High graph branch resilience; immune to branch fork contamination.
Deterministic chunking boundaries require minimal metadata overhead.
weaknesses: Fails on elliptic or anaphoric follow-up prompts ('continue', 'why?', code logs) without preceding context.
Cannot evaluate whether assistant advice was accepted, corrected, or abandoned without external turn linking.
Underperforms on Q2 (directive adaptation) and Q5 (multi-turn interpersonal interaction tracking).

evaluatedModels.modelName: Model B: Sliding Triad Window (Target Exchange bounded by 1 contextBefore and 1 contextAfter exchange)
evaluatedModels.turnWindow: 6 turns along active branch (2 contextBefore + 2 target + 2 contextAfter)
strengths: Maximizes contextual sufficiency by resolving antecedent constraints and pronouns via contextBefore.
Enables robust turn-by-turn directive-correction analysis (Q2) and downstream assumption tracing (Q3) via contextAfter.
Maintains pinpoint citation precision by restricting catalog labels strictly to the target exchange.
Deduplication rules prevent repeated context turns from inflating empirical topic weights.
weaknesses: Requires strict prompt enforcement to prevent model workers from extracting labels from context turns.
Requires branch-aware DAG traversal to assemble context along valid ancestral/descendant paths.

evaluatedModels.modelName: Model C: Macro Sub-Session (5 to 10 sequential exchanges along the branch)
strengths: Captures overarching multi-exchange workflows, complex procedural arcs, and cumulative project goals (Q1).
Preserves macro conversational momentum for chronological usage analysis (Q4).
weaknesses: Severe topic mixing and keyword dilution; multiple disparate tasks are forced into a single labeled passage.
Citation precision degrades; offsets become ambiguous across expansive turn sequences.
Fragile across conversation tree forks; creates excessive redundant overlap along shared parent nodes.
Incompatible with fine-grained Q2 correction pairs and Q5 four-layer interpersonal attribution.

comparativeAnalysisByCriterion.criterion1_ContextualSufficiency: Model A struggles with anaphoric queries unless contextBefore is supplied. Model C supplies extensive context but often introduces irrelevant historical drift. Model B achieves perfect sufficiency by providing exactly the prerequisite problem setup and immediate antecedent instructions needed for unambiguous interpretation.
comparativeAnalysisByCriterion.criterion2_TopicMixingRisk: Model A provides near-perfect isolation (5/5). Model B achieves strong isolation (4/5) provided the target boundary is strictly enforced. Model C fails (1/5) due to high topic mixing across natural user pivots within extended sessions.
comparativeAnalysisByCriterion.criterion3_CitationPrecision: Models A and B allow exact node-level and character-level pointers (5/5) because the evaluative locus is a single exchange. Model C degrades to 2/5 as citations become diffuse and multi-headed.
comparativeAnalysisByCriterion.criterion4_BranchStability: Model A is intrinsically branch-stable (5/5). Model B maintains branch stability (4/5) by following parent pointers up and child pointers down the active branch. Model C (2/5) creates combinatorial explosion and redundancy when traversing deep branching DAGs.
comparativeAnalysisByCriterion.criterion5_LabelingFeasibilityQ1toQ5: Model B is the only architecture that simultaneously supports all five analytical questions: Q1 (project goal in target + contextBefore setup), Q2 (user correction in contextAfter), Q3 (assistant claim in target + adoption in contextAfter), Q4 (turn-level interaction rigor), and Q5 (four-layer epistemic isolation).

recommendedStandard.targetScope: 1 Ordered Turn Exchange (User Prompt + Intermediate Tool Calls + Assistant Response)
recommendedStandard.contextBeforeAllocation: 1 Ancestor Exchange along active branch DAG (message.parent traversal)
recommendedStandard.contextAfterAllocation: 1 Descendant Exchange along active branch DAG
recommendedStandard.evidenceRule: Semantic labels and evidence quotes must derive 100% from the Target Exchange. Context turns provide referential awareness only.
